scope: The one component figure and this audit only; no registry, course, lesson, corpus, receiver, evidence, or other figure file was edited.
teaching_claim: Exact-frequency correlations and nearest FFT bins are different evaluations; appending 51 zeros changes the FFT sampling grid but does not turn either nearest bin into the 770 Hz or 1336 Hz physical coordinate.

implementation.root: div with role=img; no nested figure or figcaption element
implementation.layout: Three aligned cards with literal not-equal separators on desktop; the same cards and separators stack at widths at or below 650 px.
implementation.math: KaTeX via M for coordinate formulas, bin indices, frequencies, errors, percentages, and the identity condition.

palette_roles.amber: 770 Hz low tone in every coordinate family
palette_roles.blue: 1336 Hz high tone in every coordinate family
palette_roles.currentColor: coordinate-family scaffold, formulas, errors, and not-equal separators

implementation.responsive_note: At narrow widths the common sample-rate token occupies its own line, keeping the 770 Hz and 1336 Hz expressions intact.

n256.construction: the same 205 acquired samples plus 51 appended zeros

evidence_verification.identity_condition: C(f)=X_N[k] only when f=k*f_s/N under the same record and scaling convention.
evidence_verification.current_evidence_note: The N=205 values agree with evidence-preflight.json and all N=205/N=256 values were independently recomputed. Receiver-study metrics are not displayed or attributed to any of these coordinate alternatives.

defects_seen: At both narrow widths, the single header formula wrapped inside the low/high frequency expressions, separating a symbol from its value.
render_loop.fix: Split the header into three responsive KaTeX tokens; at <=650 px the sample-rate token takes a full row and the two complete tone expressions share the next row.

render_loop.verdict: PASS: no clipping, collision, broken math, mid-expression header wrap, or missing sign; all required labels and rows remain legible.
